title: Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes: The Ceiling a Valuation Is Held To
content:
Clause on the ceiling above which a valuation of a traded piece is not taken under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes. The ceiling is raised for a piece the chain itself sold, and how far depends on how long the customer has held it.

## Clause

Where the chain sold the piece and the customer has held it for at least five years, the valuation is held to the largest amount the programme answers for while a piece is in its care. Where the chain sold the piece and the customer has held it for less than five years, it is held to forty-five thousand (45000 USD). Where the chain did not sell the piece, it is held to fifteen thousand (15000 USD).

The chain sold the piece where an original sales receipt is recorded against the registration. Five years is counted as 1825 calendar days from the date the piece was originally bought, as recorded on the registration, to the handling date.

## The ceiling in figures

| Chain sold the piece | Calendar days held | Ceiling (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 1825 or more | the programme's largest amount for a piece in its care |
| yes | 1824 or fewer | 45000 |
| no | any | 15000 |

The largest amount each programme answers for while a piece is in its care is 10000 USD under the Belrose Standard Trade-In, 50000 USD under the Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee, 75000 USD under the Bridal Upgrade Guarantee, 150000 USD under the Lifetime Diamond Upgrade Guarantee, 400000 USD under the Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege and 300000 USD under the Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme.

## Day cases

- A piece the chain sold, bought exactly 1825 days ago, under the Bridal Upgrade Guarantee: the ceiling is 75000 USD.
- The same piece bought 1824 days ago: the ceiling is 45000 USD.
- A piece the chain did not sell, held for twenty years: the ceiling is 15000 USD.
